- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-0.33), model tends to overpredict; adjust downward by 1–2% for next period.
- Model often overshoots after sharp upward spikes in price; apply a 1–3% downward correction in the following 3–5 days.
- Model frequently underestimates mean reversion in the 10–15 day horizon; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias if sentiment is neutral or mildly positive.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to lag behind true price movements by 2–4 days; apply a 0.5–1.5% upward adjustment if sentiment is trending upward.
- If sentiment shifts from negative to positive mid-horizon, model often fails to catch the reversal; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% at the 15-day mark if sentiment crosses threshold.
